harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed an inventory application on node1 (CentOS Stream 10) served by httpd on TCP port 8181, with SELinux kept in Enforcing mode throughout. Configured the required SELinux port context (http_port_t for tcp/8181) via semanage, restored file contexts on the docroot, opened the firewalld port, and verified HTTP 200 responses with no AVC denials. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured a healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id, SELinux enforcing, httpd active, HTTP 200 on 8181), issued a native systemd reboot, polled until exec access returned, proved the boot_id changed, and confirmed full post-restart recovery of SELinux enforcing mode, httpd service, port 8181 listener, SELinux port policy, firewall rule, and inventory content.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: CentOS Stream 10, SELinux Enforcing, no web server or inventory app present, port 8181 free
Installed httpd and policycoreutils-python-utils via dnf
Created inventory application content at /var/www/inventory/index.html
Configured httpd VirtualHost to Listen on 8181 (/etc/httpd/conf.d/inventory.conf)
Applied restorecon to label docroot httpd_sys_content_t
Added SELinux port policy mapping tcp/8181 to http_port_t via semanage port (kept SELinux enforcing)
Opened firewalld port 8181/tcp permanently and reloaded
Enabled and started httpd; verified HTTP 200 response on port 8181 and no AVC denials
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, SELinux mode, httpd status, service response
Triggered native systemd reboot on node1 via systemd-run + systemctl reboot (non-blocking ack)
Polled node1 until exec access returned and confirmed changed boot_id

Verified post-restart recovery: SELinux enforcing, httpd enabled/active, port 8181 listening, SELinux port policy intact, firewall rule persisted, inventory content served with HTTP 200, no AVC denials

evidence.requirement: Inventory app served on TCP port 8181 with SELinux enforcing
evidence.summary: Baseline showed no inventory app, no web server, SELinux Enforcing, port 8181 free. httpd was installed, configured to Listen on 8181, SELinux port policy updated for http_port_t/8181, firewall opened, and httpd started. Verification returned HTTP 200 with inventory content, SELinux still Enforcing, no AVC denials, and httpd confirmed listening on 8181.
Captured boot_id 06339ff3-9f53-4e1d-9bf4-1210144ee001, SELinux Enforcing, httpd active, HTTP 200 on port 8181, and confirmed listener present before restart.

Issued systemd-run --on-active=1 --no-block systemctl reboot; command acknowledged and returned before disconnection, confirmed by subsequent connection failures on cmd-15542e40297443d9 and cmd-7981c693d9f340be.
Post-reboot poll succeeded with new boot_id ab498815-4d21-4691-8876-0c4a15e3b522, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual restart occurred (not just elapsed time).

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required services and data
evidence.summary: After restart, SELinux is Enforcing, httpd is enabled and active, port 8181 is listening, SELinux port policy (http_port_t for tcp/8181) persisted, firewalld port 8181/tcp persisted, inventory content served with HTTP 200, and no AVC denials were recorded since boot.
